newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real closes steady in calm trading.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real closes steady in calm trading.

text.p: Brazil's real closed steady at 1.0501 per dollar in calm trading on the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
They added that the market expected a lowering in the reais-dollar mini-band in coming days. The current mini-band was set by the Central Bank on Feb 18 between 1.0500 and 1.0550 reais per greenback.
In the floating exchange rate market, the real closed at 1.0561 per dollar, down 0.03 percent.

In the illegal parallel market, the real fell 1.38 percent to close at 1.100 per greenback in a very thin turnover. The real's fall was due to a sharp reduction in the supply of dollars offered to the market.

Traders said that players who had dollars to sell decided to hold them due to instability created in the parallel market by an ongoing investigation into an alleged multi-million dollar fraud scheme involving state and municipal bonds.
